key_insight: The LLM adapts neural-operator fine-tuning by combining a task-dependent prior with sensitivity to validation feedback, rather than relying on either alone.
engineering_relevance: For PDE model transfer, LLM-guided hyperparameter selection can outperform random search and Bayesian optimisation under tight trial budgets, making it useful for practical model adaptation workflows.
method: Tested LLM-driven configuration selection for neural operator fine-tuning across transfers within and between PDE families.
Compared held-out test nRMSE against random search and Bayesian optimisation under a limited evaluation budget.
Used controlled interventions to separate prior/task conditioning from feedback-driven decision changes.
evidence_signal: Across nearly all matched comparisons, the LLM achieved lower held-out test nRMSE, and intervention tests showed both an initial task-informed bias and feedback-sensitive proposal updates.
watch_item: The conclusions depend on the specific trial budget, transfer settings, and intervention design, so generalization to other model classes or tuning regimes still needs validation.
paper_title: Prior or Feedback? What an LLM Uses When Adapting Neural Operators
